title: Chemical Bonding
standard_text: Atoms form ionic, covalent and metallic bonds; writing formulas of ionic compounds; naming compounds; properties of ionic, covalent and metallic substances. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 4: Science of Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Science of Materials): ionic, covalent and metallic bonds, bonding and properties, writing formulae, naming compounds and ionic formulae and names. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Ionic bonds transfer electrons; covalent bonds share them.
key_sub: In a metal, positive ions sit in a sea of delocalized electrons.
body_html:
How to think about it

A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms. An ionic bond forms when a metal transfers electrons to a non-metal; the positive and negative ions attract each other. In metallic bonding, positive ions are surrounded by delocalized electrons.

The formula of an ionic compound balances the charges: Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ give MgCl₂; Al³⁺ and O²⁻ give Al₂O₃. Compounds of two elements end in -ide (sodium chloride); polyatomic ions such as SO₄²⁻ (sulfate) and NO₃⁻ (nitrate) keep their names.

Example

Formula of calcium chloride?

Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻

Answer: CaCl₂

Example

What type of bond is in H₂O?

Two non-metals

Answer: covalent

Common mistakes

  • Writing the charges in the formula (Ca²⁺Cl⁻₂).
  • Thinking ionic compounds conduct electricity when solid.
  • Calling NaCl a molecule.
